protocol: Separate prospective diagnostic after the frozen unconstrained paired-repair run. Both conditions used the same pinned model, app, public feature task, files-JSON grammar, two-call/4096-requested-output-token cap, 360-second deadline, default sampling, app verifier and 2 GiB reserve. Task-only and guided prompts differed. Negative control failed and assistant-authored positive control passed before inference. Generated source and raw responses remain opt-in in the local private report.
interpretation: Grammar produced parseable file envelopes for the completed pair, but neither condition passed both TypeScript and app tests. The selected task-only candidate passed tests but failed TypeScript because its public interface omitted hasProduct. The guided candidate failed TypeScript and tests; its repair also failed and was rejected. The resource guard then stopped a subsequent call after the memory observation changed, with available budget falling below the reserved 2 GiB. Four planned trials were not run. No feature improvement or qualification is established.
limitations: Only one completed pair on a public development task. Grammar constrains the JSON envelope, not code correctness. The earlier unconstrained run is not a causal comparator because this is a separate stochastic run with different output constraints. No private held-out tasks, native build of generated code, human correction, model input-token/cost accounting, independent review or customer acceptance. Keep this failed/incomplete evidence visible; do not lower gates or alter customer grants. Core/Admin unchanged; no package release.
